dm-sans.$description: Named for the FACE, not for the job it does. `--font-sans` (tier 2) is the token that points here — a spoke swapping to a serif re-points that, and this token keeps meaning what it says.

400.$description: The full standard 100–900 ramp is carried here even where the hub face has no use for a step, alongside the three half-steps DM Sans's variable axis does use (350/550/650). A spoke on a different family re-points the tier-2 named steps onto its own weights — cb-fish's IBM Plex remap needs 400 and 600, and neither existed until this ramp was completed. (Note: the group-level $description slot is taken by semantic/typography.json — Style Dictionary merges group nodes across files and collides on it — which is why this rationale hangs off a leaf.)

font-style.$description: The finite option set, so a composite can reference the value rather than spelling the keyword. `italic` has 4 literal uses in the kit today.

line-height.$description: Unitless, so it inherits as a ratio rather than a computed length. `$type: number` (not `other`) so the set can export to Figma as line-height rather than as an opaque string.

none.$description: No leading — the box supplies the height. Badges, pills, chips, buttons, kbd, avatars, icons: single-line control labels where any leading would misalign the text in its box.

tight.$description: Headings, and the small helper and label text that sits close to its control — field errors, checkbox and radio labels, combobox and input-tag entries. A `snug` rung at 1.4 briefly sat between this and `normal`; it was folded in here. Four rungs is the scale — a fifth was a value looking for a reason.

text-transform.$description: The finite option set. `uppercase` is read by the .typography-eyebrow composite and by four components.
